population.note: FICTIONAL. Ever-used minus current is 30.0 − 20.2 = 9.8% of adults who used and are off now. New ever-users since 2030 are 3.5 pts: 2.6 on and 0.9 already off. Of the 26.5 pts who had used by 2030, 17.6 are on and 8.9 are off. On: 2.6 + 17.6 = 20.2. Off: 0.9 + 8.9 = 9.8. Within the 2030 cohort, 10.5 of the 18.8 then on stayed on (56% two-year persistence, up from 50% because daily pills are easier to continue). The other 8.3 stopped and joined the 7.7 already off, a pool of 16.0. Of that pool 7.1 restarted (44% over two years, down from 55% because employers dropped coverage). 10.5 + 7.1 = 17.6. Cycled: 8.9 pts had cycled by 2030; about 3.0 pts of the 7.1 restarters are first-time restarts; 11.9 / 30.0 = 40%. This excludes pill 'weekend-off' skipping, which is not a stop. Users are ≈54.5M of ~270M adults. Age bands weighted by adult shares (20/33/24/23%) give 2.2 + 7.1 + 7.7 + 3.2 = 20.2. Income thirds average (26 + 19.6 + 15)/3 = 20.2. Bottom-third use rose because the HRSA programme grew and cash pills start at $149. Middle-third growth slowed because employers retreated, and many middle-third users moved to cash pills. 65+ rose to 14% (~8.7M) through the cheaper Bridge and oral starts. Off-drug adults: ~26.5M who used and stopped, plus ~189M who never used. The never-used now include a visible group who refuse on principle (see the backlash), as well as the uninsured who cannot pay cash. Pediatric: ~1.0% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 730k, of whom ≈130k are aged 6–11, mostly on generic liraglutide plus some off-label oral semaglutide. The first 2012-era adolescent users are now in their mid-twenties, with about 9 years of exposure.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge extended in Dec 2031 through 2033. Payment falls from $275 to $245 a month under a negotiated deal tied to oral volume, with the $50 copay and the 65+ DEXA/strength counselling visit unchanged. About 2.8M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 2.8M × $245 × 12 ≈ $8.2B/yr. Medicare overall pays ≈16.7% of incretin fills ≈ 9.1M users (8.7M aged 65+ plus ~0.4M disabled under-65). Medicaid pays ≈11.6% ≈ 6.3M at $245: 6.3M × $245 × 12 ≈ $18.5B/yr, federal and state combined. The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged, and Missouri's was approved in 2031. HRSA Community Incretin Access Program FY2032 ($4.6B appropriation, renewed annually): 2.3M on generic liraglutide × $70 × 12 ≈ $1.93B, plus 1.4M on oral semaglutide for cessation/AUD × $149 × 12 ≈ $2.50B, total ≈ $4.43B for 3.7M users. The DoD Force Readiness Metabolic Program covers ~140k active-duty members: 140k × $149 × 12 ≈ $0.25B. The VA (AUD) and state public-safety programmes cover another ~0.46M.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India sells generic tirzepatide (launched 2031, $30–70/month) and 80+ semaglutide brands at $6–40. Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and China sell generic injectable and oral semaglutide. US generic semaglutide ANDAs hold tentative approval, but patent settlements set the first entry date at March 2033.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~54.5M users: commercial 29.4% (16.0M), Medicare 16.7% (9.1M), Medicaid 11.6% (6.3M), HRSA free provision 6.8% (3.7M), DoD/VA/public-safety 1.1% (0.6M), cash/direct 18.9% (10.3M), gray 15.6% (8.5M) = 100.1% (rounding). Commercial users fell from 17.8M to 16.0M as employers dropped weight-only coverage (57% → 44% cover weight management). About 70% of remaining commercial fills now sit under diabetes, CV, OSA, CKD, or the mandated cessation/AUD codes. Cash grew from 7.0M to 10.3M. Most of that growth is the employer-dropped middle third buying pills on TrumpRx. Managed decline: TrumpRx semaglutide pen falls from $349 to $249, tirzepatide from $449 to $299, oral semaglutide/Foundayo starting doses from $199 to $149, and oral semaglutide 50 mg maintenance to $199. Wegovy list is still $1,349. Retatrutide allocation ended in mid-2032 but it still has no cash-portal price at $1,499 list, and concierge practices bill it through employer carve-outs. MariTide (monthly) lists at $1,299 and is mostly uncovered. Oral formulations are ≈52% of users and ≈70% of new starts. Gray market shrank from 9.0M to 8.5M because the $149 legal pill undercut the $99–199 compounded vials. Indian mail pens and research-use retatrutide persist.

GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg high dose, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo, incl. post-injectable maintenance label)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)
GIPR antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody-peptide, monthly injectable (maritide, Sep 2031)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, MASH F2–F3 only, Jun 2032)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, Apr 2029)
alcohol use disorder (semaglutide, Jun 2030; extended to oral semaglutide 2031)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'weekend-off' and 'Friday skip' pill regimens to recover appetite, libido or pleasure
oral semaglutide for ages 6–11 under pediatric endocrinology (only liraglutide is labelled)
'calm/focus' low-dose subscriptions, shrunk to ~1M users after the anhedonia label and FTC consent orders

gambling and cannabis reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Oral parity is realised with what the approval rules allow: an existing product in a new form, not a new molecule. FDA approved high-dose oral semaglutide 50 mg in May 2031 on a 72-week head-to-head showing 16.4% mean loss, non-inferior to injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg (15.8%). It also added orforglipron's maintenance label: users switched from injectable tirzepatide kept ~90% of their loss at one year. No pill matches tirzepatide or retatrutide on loss from start. Parity holds against the most-prescribed injectable and for maintenance, and that removed the needle as the reason not to start. MariTide (BLA Jul 2030) was approved Sep 2031. Survodutide (resubmitted) was approved Jun 2032 for MASH only, with hepatic monitoring; the obesity claim was not granted. Amycretin's resubmission was accepted Sep 2032 after reinspection of the facility, with a decision in 2033. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3 and are not on the market. A semaglutide sNDA for ages 6–11 was filed Nov 2031 and is still under review. The incretin market is ≈$132B in 2032, roughly flat: US volume is up ~9% and US net price down ~14%, with ex-US generic erosion.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Oral starts have similar GI rates at equivalent exposure.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed gastric emptying on drug is established; persistence after stopping is still disputed. MDL 3094 has ~55,000 filed and tolled claims. The second bellwether (Feb 2031) was a defence verdict, and a third (2032) went for the plaintiff.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled. FDA still declines a persistent-gastroparesis label. Global settlement talks under a special master have not concluded.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss. Absolute numbers keep rising with retatrutide and research-peptide use.
Pooled long-term data show no causal confirmation and a low absolute risk. Claims remain in the MDL.
Remains a population problem in 65+. Worst in unmonitored low-efficacy users and in cash pill users without counselling.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label (2028) stands. The Bridge counselling visit continues. HRSA and the cash portal have no body-composition requirement. The DoD programme requires a quarterly fitness test.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: HR ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term and cycling users, concentrated in women. Interim one-year data from the liraglutide 6–11 bone-accrual study (2032) show no significant difference but are underpowered.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA recommended in 65+ and postmenopausal women. The pediatric registry continues, with a full readout due 2034.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare'; FDA warnings mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, now examined separately from anhedonia in the retatrutide postmarketing data.

Validated retatrutide and semaglutide postmarketing studies (2031): clinically meaningful anhedonia on SHAPS in 7.8% vs 2.9% placebo at the top retatrutide dose, and 4.6% vs 2.7% on semaglutide 2.4 mg/oral 50 mg. Self-reported reduced pleasure in 10–15% of long-term users. Dose-dependent and reversible within ~2–4 weeks of stopping.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling change (Mar 2031) adds 'Anhedonia and emotional blunting' to Warnings and Precautions with a prevalence table and a 'consider dose reduction' instruction. FTC consent orders bar unlabelled 'calm/focus' claims. The FAA adds an anhedonia screen to medical certification for pilots on incretins.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Structural stops increased: employer coverage terminations at 2032 plan-year renewal, the cessation cap and waiver lockouts.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation ongoing; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Signals for iron, B12, vitamin D and protein insufficiency persist in older and low-income users.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of adult follow-up and nine adolescent. ~130k children aged 6–11 are on a drug, with no pubertal-timing data beyond trial length.
Poison-centre calls are flat to slightly down since 2030 as the cheap legal pill displaces vials. Research-use retatrutide harms persist in gyms.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning letters and import alerts continue; still no prosecution of individuals.

safety_ledger.effect: Restart GI events after self-directed drug holidays
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Pharmacovigilance and ED reports of vomiting and dehydration when users restart oral semaglutide 50 mg or high-dose orforglipron at full dose after multi-day breaks. Concentrated in 'weekend-off' and anniversary-holiday users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA safety communication (2032) on re-titration after more than 3 missed days; no label change yet.

food_and_beverage.state: Volume losses continue at a slower rate because adoption grew only ~1.4 pts. Snacks and sugary drinks are still down. Protein, fibre and 'pill-companion' formats are mature. A small 'unmedicated' indulgence niche (heritage baking, full-sugar soda revivals) is marketed to the backlash crowd.

alcohol.state: Oral semaglutide for AUD under parity and HRSA keeps cutting into heavy-drinker volume. Spirits are down again but less sharply. Brewers report a 'Saturday bump' in high-uptake states, attributed to pill users skipping a dose.

restaurants.state: Smaller-plate menus and two-menu weddings are now standard. Value buffets keep closing in mid-income suburbs. Weekend brunch traffic rises relative to weekday dinner.

apparel.state: Size runs stay wide. Plus-size brands stabilise and market to the fat-acceptance revival as a choice rather than a residual. Athletic-cut tailoring is still the top-third growth segment.

fitness.state: Strength-and-DEXA studios keep expanding. Low-cost gyms gain cash-pill members. Military base gyms run mandated strength blocks for programme enrollees.

insurance.state: Employers that cover weight management fell from 57% to 44%. Coverage concentrates on diabetes, cardiac, OSA, CKD and mandated cessation/AUD codes. Pharmacy trend slows to ~+7% because of exclusions and lower net prices. Indication-shopping audits on AUDIT scores are routine.

pharma.state: Volume up, US net price down ~14%. Lilly leads on oral orforglipron. Novo's oral 50 mg win offsets its injectable exposure ahead of 2033 generic entry. MDL reserves are rising. Generic liraglutide contractors are squeezed at a $70 HRSA price.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Pills cannot be seen, so the molecule can no longer be guessed. What shows is muscle (paid coaching) and the deliberately unmedicated heavier body, which now reads as a stance as often as a circumstance.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: 'The Charlotte build' persists among top-third men. The middle third lost employer coverage and bought $149–199 pills, so thinness spread but muscle did not. The class line is now coaching and DEXA, not thinness.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Weekend family meals are larger because many pill users skip Friday or Saturday doses. Pediatricians discuss 'kid portions' for the ~130k children aged 6–11 on drug. Churches in the Full Table movement hold monthly communal suppers framed as an act of faith.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles now list 'on / off / weekends off'. 'Unmedicated' is a stated preference in some apps, mostly among Gen Z women in Atlanta and Austin associated with the fat-acceptance revival.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: A contested field. The clinical frame (appetite as a variable) still dominates, but the backlash reframes desire as part of the self or a gift from God, and the anhedonia label gave it a citation.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Labelled since Mar 2031: clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~4.6% (semaglutide) to 7.8% (top-dose retatrutide), against 2.7–2.9% on placebo; self-reported reduced pleasure in 10–15% of long-term users. Surveys find ~38% of oral users deliberately skip doses at least monthly, mostly weekends. 'Calm/focus' subscriptions fell from ~1.5–2M to ~1M after the label and FTC orders.
interior_life.framing: A side effect people manage. 'The grey' is now everyday speech, and 'taking the weekend' is what people do about it. Clinicians write 'dose reduction for blunting' in charts. Wellness brands that had sold it as a feature rebranded to 'gentle-dose'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employers dropped 'focus' perks after the label. Weekly-pen workers used to time holidays to pitches; now daily-pill workers skip a day for client dinners or creative sprints. Service members in the DoD programme cannot take holidays, because adherence is a readiness metric. Pilots answer an anhedonia screen. The union contract language barring employer access to PBM adherence data holds and has spread to two more contracts.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' is no longer a niche label. Comedians do 'Saturday sets'. Full Table worship music and fat-acceptance zines form a small, visible counterculture. Sports-betting handle is up modestly on weekends.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples schedule sex on skip days. Therapists ask 'Which days are you on?'. Mismatched holiday schedules are a common complaint.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The anhedonia label armed the backlash: anti-pharma 'natural body' activists and Southern Baptist leaders cite it, as do some progressive fat-acceptance groups, which makes for odd coalitions. Tennessee passed a parental-consent and second-opinion law for under-12 prescribing. Candidates are asked whether they are 'on' and whether their kids are.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access on oral forms and price, and more candid on safety: the anhedonia class label, the re-titration communication, MASH-only survodutide. The FTC polices wellness claims through consent orders. Gray-market enforcement stays symbolic.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: HRSA programme renewed for FY2032 at $4.6B (≈$4.43B committed). Bridge extended at $245/$50. The ACA cessation mandate and AUD parity continue. No civilian mandate to take the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The Indiana, Arkansas and now Missouri waivers require ≥80% PDC and weigh-ins. HRSA requires only refill pickup. The DoD programme tracks adherence and body composition in readiness systems, the strongest conditioning regime in the country, and it is voluntary only in name for members flagged by tape tests.
state.workforce_or_military: FY2032 NDAA (Dec 2031) created the DoD Force Readiness Metabolic Program: oral incretins for active-duty members who fail body-composition standards, ~140k enrolled at ≈$0.25B/yr. The FAA's Dec 2031 guidance lets pilots fly on stable oral or injectable semaglutide/tirzepatide after 3 months, subject to an anhedonia screen. Texas, Florida, Oklahoma and nine other states fund oral incretins for police, fire and 911 dispatchers through public-safety wellness grants. DOT apnea clearance still pushes tirzepatide on truckers. The VA continues AUD use.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 tariffs remain, but domestic oral fill lines (Lilly in Indiana and North Carolina) reduce exposure to them. Indian generic tirzepatide exports by mail are a new trade irritant. The 2033 US generic semaglutide entry date shapes Novo's pricing.

events.event: FDA orders class labelling change adding 'Anhedonia and emotional blunting' to Warnings and Precautions for all incretin weight and AUD products, with a prevalence table from validated postmarketing studies; FTC follows with consent orders against six 'calm/focus' telehealth brands

FDA approves 50 mg oral semaglutide after a 72-week head-to-head shows non-inferiority to injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg (16.4% vs 15.8%), and adds an orforglipron maintenance claim for patients switching off injectable tirzepatide

Southern Baptist Convention adopts a resolution warning against 'pharmaceutical suppression of God-given desire' in children; Tulsa-born Full Table church suppers spread to ~1,200 congregations as Atlanta fat-acceptance groups stage 'Unmedicated' rallies; Tennessee later enacts second-opinion rules for under-12 prescribing

Mercer survey for 2032 plan year: employers covering weight-only incretin use fall to 44%, as CalPERS and several Fortune 100 self-insured plans keep only diabetes, cardiac, OSA and mandated cessation/AUD codes

FY2032 NDAA creates the DoD Force Readiness Metabolic Program covering oral incretins for active-duty members failing body-composition standards; FAA issues pilot guidance permitting stable incretin use with an anhedonia screen

TrumpRx cuts cash prices to $249 (semaglutide pen), $299 (tirzepatide) and $149 for oral starting doses, and Congress extends the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through 2033 at $245/month with the $50 copay intact

open_tensions: Generic semaglutide is set to enter the US in March 2033 under settlement. The $245 Bridge, the $149 HRSA contracts and Novo's oral strategy are all priced against a market that is about to reprice.

The state now pays for soldiers, pilots and police to take the drug as readiness infrastructure while private employers drop coverage. The working middle third pays cash, and the strictest adherence surveillance falls on people in uniform.

Anhedonia is labelled and dose-dependent, yet the same reward modulation is the mechanism of the AUD and cessation approvals the state funds. Daily pills turned drug holidays into routine self-dosing, with a new restart-GI signal.

The backlash has a legislative foothold on children: ~130k 6–11-year-olds are on drug, a semaglutide 6–11 sNDA is under review, the bone-accrual readout is not due until 2034, and Tennessee-style consent laws are spreading.
still_true: Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation for two 90-day courses a year.
The HRSA Community Incretin Access Program is still a discretionary grant programme renewed annually, and its sites still require only refill pickup, not weigh-ins.

prose.headline: The Weekend Off: The Pill Now Works Like the Shot, the Label Admits the Grey, and America Learns to Skip Saturdays
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 about one American adult in five takes an incretin drug, roughly fifty-four million people. That is up only a little from two years ago, but the drug is taken differently now. Most users swallow it. In May 2031 the FDA approved a 50-milligram semaglutide tablet on a head-to-head trial showing it worked as well as the weekly injection most Americans had been using. Lilly's orforglipron won a label for keeping weight off after people switch from tirzepatide pens. No pill yet matches retatrutide, which is still the drug of the coached and the rich. For most people, though, the needle stopped being a reason to say no. Seven new starts in ten are now oral.

Prices came down through negotiation rather than competition. The federal cash portal charges $149 to start a pill, $249 for a semaglutide pen and $299 for tirzepatide. Medicare's Bridge was extended through 2033 at $245 a month, and the copay is still fifty dollars. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349, and nobody pays it. Generic semaglutide is approved on paper but held back by a settlement until March 2033, and every price in the system is set with that date in mind.

Employers moved the other way. Fewer than half now cover the drug for weight alone. Plans pay when the claim code says diabetes, heart, sleep apnea, kidney, smoking or alcohol, and auditors look hard at the alcohol claims. The middle third lost its coverage and moved to the cash pill. Free provision at community health centres reaches 3.7 million people, still on a grant renewed one year at a time. The gray market shrank slightly because a legal pill at $149 is hard to undercut. People in uniform get the drug from the state. Under the December 2031 defence bill, about 140,000 service members who fail their tape test are enrolled, and their adherence is logged as a readiness metric. Twelve states pay for it for police, firefighters and 911 dispatchers. Pilots can now fly on it once they pass a screen.

The screen exists because of the label. In March 2031 the FDA added anhedonia and emotional blunting to every incretin's warnings, with a table: under five percent above placebo on semaglutide, about five percent on the top retatrutide dose, dose-dependent and reversible. The wellness brands that sold 'quiet' rebranded or folded. What had been a marketed feature became an ordinary complaint, and the daily pill made the remedy easy: skip a day. More than a third of pill users skip deliberately, mostly Fridays and Saturdays. Brewers report a Saturday bump. Brunch is busier than weekday dinner. Couples schedule sex on skip days. Emergency rooms see people who restarted at full dose on Monday and spent the night vomiting, and the FDA has issued a safety communication about it.

The label also gave a cause its citation. In Tulsa, church suppers called Full Table spread to more than a thousand congregations, built on the claim that appetite is a gift. The Southern Baptist Convention warned against suppressing it in children. In Atlanta, young women revived fat acceptance under the word 'unmedicated', and plus-size brands that had been shrinking began selling to them as a choice. Tennessee now requires a second opinion before a child under twelve is prescribed the drug. About 130,000 children that age take it, and the bone study that might reassure their parents reports in 2034.

The lawsuits grind on in Philadelphia, now 55,000 claims, with one defence verdict and two plaintiff wins. From outside, the country looks steadier, leaner and more sober. Up close, many people are taking a little less than prescribed on the days they want to feel something.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Okafor sets the white tablet on the counter at 5:40 and takes it with four ounces of water, thirty minutes before coffee, as the leaflet says. The leaflet has a new box now. She read it once, in the parking lot of the Walgreens on Admiral.

The city's public-safety wellness grant pays for it. It is the reason she can afford a pill her old insurer stopped covering the year Marcus's company dropped theirs. Nineteen years on the 911 floor in Tulsa. Twelve-hour shift.

At 2 p.m. a man calls about his wife, who isn't breathing. Denise talks him through compressions in a voice so level it frightens her afterward. She eats half a turkey wrap at her console and throws the rest away.

Her daughter texts: Full Table at church Sunday?? Bring the peach thing.

The peach thing is her mother's cobbler. Denise hasn't wanted it in two years. She hasn't wanted much.

At home Marcus is watching the Thunder with the sound off. He went off his pen in March. It was cash and he was tired of it. The weight is coming back slowly at his belt, and he laughs more. She notices that she notices.

She opens the blister pack and looks at Saturday.

The program logs refills, not days. Her supervisor can't see it; the union made sure of that. But the leaflet says to call a doctor if she skips more than three.

Saturday she leaves the tablet in its foil. Sunday she makes the cobbler, and at the long tables in the fellowship hall she eats a whole square, slowly, and tastes the nutmeg.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Brewers report a 'Saturday bump' in high-uptake states, attributed to pill users skipping a dose.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a one-day skip of a daily GLP-1 or orforglipron pill leaves most of the drug effect in place because of long half-lives, so a measurable regional alcohol bump is asserted rather than shown. The same objection applies to skip days restoring 'pleasure' and to the restart-GI signal.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The first 2012-era adolescent users are now in their mid-twenties, with about 9 years of exposure.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: it is internally inconsistent. Adolescent incretin use began around 2020-23, so 2012 is wrong, and 9 years of exposure does not match someone in their mid-twenties from a 2012 start.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Oral formulations are ≈52% of users and ≈70% of new starts.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: reaching a majority of about 54.5M users on pills in two years, from a 'mixed' route in 2030, means converting well over 15M existing injectable users. The world shows only 3.5 pts of new ever-users and no switching flow to support it.

rationale.badness: Use is slightly higher at 20.2%, and pills and lower prices widen access. Offsetting that, the DoD tape-test enrolment with adherence logged as a readiness metric (the 'voluntary only in name' regime), employer retreat that pushes the middle third to cash, and ~130k children aged 6-11 on drug with bone data not due until 2034 make it a recognisably harder society. The anhedonia label makes the main harm nameable and measured, which lowers the epistemic score. The overall level is a modest step beyond 2030, not a collapse.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible in fields and dated events. Adoption is +1.4 pts, managed decline is the 2032-01 price cut, employer coverage falls 57% to 44%, and the anhedonia label, oral 50 mg parity, backlash, DoD/FAA/public-safety programmes and the pediatric sNDA are all present; market_shock is none. mechanism: Most chains are shown, such as employer drop to cash pill and pill to weekend skipping. Claims 1 and 2 are weak: the pharmacology of skip days and the Saturday brewer bump, and the '2012-era adolescent' error. The anhedonia label also arrives within months of data the start world said was due in 2031. magnitude: Everything sits inside the envelope (20.2% on, 30.0% ever). The population arithmetic, age and income averages, payer mix (100.1%), Medicare/Medicaid/HRSA/DoD spending, pediatric counts and approval timing all reconcile. The only soft point is claim 3, the 52% oral share, which has no switching flow behind it.

least_plausible_claims.quote: the daily pill made the remedy easy: skip a day
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the world's own ledger says anhedonia is 'reversible within ~2–4 weeks of stopping', so skipping one day should not restore pleasure or appetite. Oral semaglutide also has a roughly week-long half-life. The whole weekend-off economy (brewers' Saturday bump, larger weekend meals, Denise tasting nutmeg after one skipped tablet) rests on this asserted effect.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The first 2012-era adolescent users are now in their mid-twenties, with about 9 years of exposure.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: this contradicts its own 'about 9 years' of exposure, since 2012 would give 20 years, and the parent's 7 years of adolescent exposure in 2030. A person who was an adolescent in 2012 would be in their early thirties in 2032, not their mid-twenties.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Gray market shrank from 9.0M to 8.5M because the $149 legal pill undercut the $99–199 compounded vials.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: $149 does not undercut vials priced from $99. The cheaper Indian pens ($8–45) and research-peptide vials persist, so the stated cause for the shrinkage is asserted rather than shown.

rationale.badness: The world is a recognisably harder version of 2030. Employer coverage falls to 44% and the middle third pays cash. The DoD program logs adherence for service members flagged by tape tests, which is the strictest conditioning regime in the country. Pediatric use grows to 130k with bone data not due until 2034, and sarcopenia and fracture risk persist in 65+ users. Offsetting this, the anhedonia harm is now labelled and measured, which lowers the epistemic score, and cheaper pills widen access. The cohesion cost is real but modest: backlash politics and schedules built around skip days.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised and traceable to events.
